A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “chiral” spin of the proton is about 0.3 and the “invariant” one is about 0, which is compatible with the absence of polarized strange in the proton.

the invariant spin of the proton, as determined by the quark and gluon distributions, is about 50% larger than the chiral spin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chiral spin sum rule is violated at leading order in the large N_c expansion, while the invariant spin sum rule is satisfied.
the invariant spin of the nucleon is a more natural and fundamental quantity than the chiral spin, and that the latter is not a gauge invariant quantity.
invariant spin, which is the spin of the proton at short distances, is a more fundamental concept than the spin carried by the quarks and the antiquarks.
